question: A 38-year-old man comes to the physician because of white lesions in his mouth for 4 days. He also has intense pain while chewing food. He was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma around 8 months ago. He is undergoing chemotherapy and is currently on his fourth cycle. He was treated for herpes labialis 4 months ago with acyclovir. He has smoked half a pack of cigarettes daily for 15 years. He appears healthy. Vital signs are within normal limits. Cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy is present. Oral examination shows white plaques on his tongue and buccal mucosa that bleed when scraped off. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the next best step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Immunosuppression due to chemotherapy -> increased risk of opportunistic infections -> possible oral candidiasis -> 70% CHAIN: Presence of white plaques in the mouth -> suspicion of oral thrush -> 80% CHAIN: History of herpes labialis -> previous antiviral treatment with acyclovir -> unlikely to be herpes -> 90% CHAIN: Bleeding when white plaques are scraped off -> suggests candidiasis -> 80% CHAIN: Cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy -> concern for lymphoma progression or infection -> 70% CHAIN: Next best step in management -> Culture of the lesions -> 70%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with white lesions in the mouth, history of chemotherapy-induced immunosuppression, and previous treatment with acyclovir for herpes labialis raise suspicion for oral candidiasis. Given the concern for opportunistic infections, the next best step in management is to culture the lesions to confirm the diagnosis and guide appropriate treatment.
analysis: The patient's presentation with white lesions in the mouth, history of chemotherapy-induced immunosuppression, and previous treatment with acyclovir for herpes labialis raise suspicion for oral candidiasis, an opportunistic infection. Given this context, the next best step in management is to culture the lesions to confirm the diagnosis and guide appropriate treatment.
